exceptions.justification: generateEnvManifest sorts every variable and declaration by key so the manifest and the compatibility findings are byte-stable between runs; that sort makes the whole-project run grow as n log n. The last release's committed results measured it close to linear (exponent 0.89); a local run of this change measured 1.14 (linearithmic).
exceptions.ruleBroken: Manifest generation grows linearly with the number of variables.
exceptions.attempted: Looked for a way to keep deterministic output without the sort; the keys arrive in discovery order, which depends on the file system, so a stable order needs one.
exceptions.constraint: The manifest and the compatibility findings must be identical for the same sources on every machine, and the file system does not promise an order.
exceptions.whyPreferable: A linear pass over unsorted data would make the generated manifest differ between machines and between runs, which would break reproducible builds and cause noisy diffs, for a gain of a logarithmic factor.
exceptions.residualRisk: At very large contract counts the sort's share of the build time grows; at the ladder's largest size, 5,120 variables, the local run measured an exponent of 1.14.
exceptions.revisitWhen: A single project routinely declares more than 100,000 variables, or the next release measures an exponent above 1.3.

exceptions.justification: processors.toArray is unchanged by this change: it splits the string once and runs the element processor on each field, linear by construction. CI's pull-request run measured an exponent of 1.20 (linearithmic) where the last release measured 0.86 (linear), on a shared GitHub-hosted runner; accepted as run-to-run noise by the maintainer's decision to release.
exceptions.ruleBroken: A benchmark's growth class must not get worse than at the last release without a person's acceptance.
exceptions.attempted: Checked that src/helpers and src/runtime are unchanged against main, so no code in this change can have altered toArray's cost.
exceptions.constraint: Growth classes are fitted on one CI run on a shared runner, where a near-boundary exponent can cross a class line between runs.
exceptions.whyPreferable: Rewriting a linear split to chase one run's fit would change nothing real; the next measured run either confirms linear or keeps this record honest.
exceptions.residualRisk: A real regression in toArray would be hidden for as long as this record stands.
exceptions.revisitWhen: The post-merge benchmark run measures toArray again; remove this record if it is linear there.
